answer: Verification runs against the issuer's own registry every epoch, so a forged entry is caught on the next check. The defence rests on hGV licence tenure with tachograph record history: tachographs filed under one licence for years. The price is per head, and the karst test proves it: Forging 124 of these means building 124 separate tachograph records from scratch, and years of history cannot be bought in bulk. The ferrous trail is public, the timber check is cheap to run, and a farm of 124 aliases pays 124 full fares while the honest agent pays one.
